### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via installCommentAccessHooks (symbol, a top-level function), checkControlledByParentWrite (literal, a string literal in AttachmentSecurityLike; a string literal in CommentSecurityLike))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0b28161cfcb5595561d30de1a8de09c6ac99179a` — the merge of head `7deb8468f840b8b979a5e8ab0fe1b206faf78abd` into base `b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0b28161cfcb5595561d30de1a8de09c6ac99179a && git checkout 0b28161cfcb5595561d30de1a8de09c6ac99179a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834 7deb8468f840b8b979a5e8ab0fe1b206faf78abd && git checkout -B drift-repro b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834 && git merge --no-ff 7deb8468f840b8b979a5e8ab0fe1b206faf78abd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7deb8468f840b8b979a5e8ab0fe1b206faf78abd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-parent-update-parity.test.ts + .changeset/24549-parent-gate-parity.md, content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-attachment-service.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts, packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts, packages/core/src/security/operation-private-keys.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Inputs, as the brief sets out: card #24549 (body and its three comments), PR #24641 (body, six-file list, the net diff against `main` at the head), and the 41 check-runs on the head — 36 `success`, 5 `skipped` (the main-only battery), none failed; the five required contexts are among the green. The disclosure ruling quoted on the card (#9387) holds in this record: it judges the invariant and the code's shape, and names no caller shape, grant or record that the gates used to admit.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing on every parent-EDIT limb of both gates — right.** `mayEditAttachmentParent` (the attach rule, the parent-editor limb of the row rule on update and delete, the attach rule on a re-point, and `FileAttachmentService.assertMayAttach`, which hands `getSecurity` into the same function) and the comment kit's `canEditParent` (the author-or-parent-editor limb on update and delete) each run the pre-existing step — record sharing, or the degraded caller-scoped read, then the master-detail check — and only on an admit ask `security.explain` for `update` on the parent `(object, recordId)`, admitting on `allowed === true` and `record.visible === true` both. The step runs last and answers `false` or rejects; it never answers `true` where the first step refused, so what is admitted after is a subset of what was admitted before: a narrowing, never a widening.
2. **That verdict IS the by-id update judgement — right.** `explain.zod.ts` defines `record.visible` as whether the operation is permitted on this specific record after all layers (`decidedBy` spans `object_crud`, `owd_baseline`, `depth`, `sharing`, `rls` and the rest), and the record path in `security-plugin.ts` (its #19963 note) computes a record-grained write verdict from the by-id write path's own inputs, so `record.visible` for `update` is the answer the by-id PATCH gives, the ADR-0055 master gate included. With no `userId` on the request the principal explained is the context handed in, so the `manage_users` gate is never tripped. The card's invariant is held by the write path's own composition; neither gate keeps a copy of it.
3. **The envelope handed to `explain` — right.** Both kits pass `callerContext(ctx)`, which is `withoutOperationPrivateKeys` over the operation context: a fresh copy with every `__`-prefixed key removed, the envelope the sharing step already receives (the full-envelope ruling on `ISharingService`), so explain's own `__writeScope` stamp lands on its copy and never on the caller's request context. Pinned in both suites (the context handed over carries no `__writeScope`).
4. **A decision carrying no `record` verdict refuses — right.** A decision that did not judge the record is not an admit; fail-closed, pinned per gate.
5. **Rejections propagate unchanged — right; one answer changes, as declared.** A store fault keeps its status (pinned: a 503 stays a 503, never an admit, never a 403). `explain-engine.ts` throws `ExplainObjectNotFoundError` (`404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`) for a name the registry does not hold, so an attach naming such a parent object now answers what a by-id update of it answers, in place of the `403 FILES_DISABLED` the `enable.files` capability gate (plugin-audit `audit-writers.ts`, registered on the same `beforeInsert`) answered first. Both are refusals, and the new one discloses only what a by-id update already discloses. Which of the two a caller sees depends on the cross-plugin order of the two hooks on that event, which this diff does not pin; the changeset, the PR body and the docs page state the 404 as measured on the real stack.
6. **Public surface: `AttachmentSecurityLike` and `CommentSecurityLike` (both barrel-exported) gain an optional `explain` — right, additive.** Every supplier that conformed before still conforms; no member is removed or re-typed. `FileAttachmentServiceDeps.getSecurity`'s own intersection with the same optional member becomes redundant and is unchanged. Known and accepted: `explain` is NOT optional on `ISecurityService` (the contract says so beside `canReadObject`), so the `Partial` spelling is the availability rule's feature detection, not a contract change; on a composed stack the kernel's `security` service (plugin-security) serves it, and both real compositions (`storage-service-plugin.ts`, `audit-plugin.ts`) resolve that service into the gates, so the not-asked branch is unreachable there. A non-conforming service that omits it would be judged by the first step alone — stated in both module headers, the posture `assertMayAttach` already takes for its own `explain` question.
7. **Edit depth — right, and the restrictive divergence is preserved, not widened.** The sharing step stays asked at `own` (the #7144 ruling recorded on `ISharingService`: the parent gates STAY at `own`; an accepted ruling binds until superseded, Prime Directive #13). The new step composes after it, so on those rows the gate still refuses where the parent's update and `explain` admit. Carried to ③.
8. **Not changed, rightly:** posting a comment and moving a comment stay read rules on the parent (the card's invariant is the parent-EDIT gates); the system session returns before any step, so rows 9b and 45 of `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` (the advisory drift hit) stay accurate; `plugin-security` and `packages/spec` are untouched.
9. **Pins — right for what they can hold under the disclosure ruling.** Per gate, one row per shape of sharing verdict, master outcome and update judgement, each refusal asserted on its ADR-0112 envelope (`code` and `status`), plus the asks-once, author-exempt and uploader-exempt, not-visible, store-fault, no-sharing-service and no-security-service rows. The report cites the pins red first on the unfixed gates (attachment 38 failed / 29 passed; comment 20 failed / 12 passed) and an ablation on the final head red on the same rows; `Test Core` is green on this head. The attachment rows live in the existing file so they drive its ledgered engine double (`check:engine-double-contract` green). The real-stack half — `explain`'s update verdict equals the by-id update — is held by `plugin-security/src/explain-enforce-parity.test.ts`, present at the head; a real-stack pin inside the gate packages is deferred (③).
10. **Docs — right at the head.** `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx` now states the invariant, the three-question order, the depth caveat, the re-point and comment-kit parity, and the two refusal codes; its rows match the code read above.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/24549-parent-gate-parity.md`: `@objectstack/service-storage: minor` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit: minor` — the two packages the diff publishes from (both at `18.0.0-next.5`); nothing else in the diff publishes. **Right.**
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset — a truthful `no` to the widening question, and a narrowing of a runtime accept set, so BREAKING. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (#16421) grades a declared narrowing `minor` inside the launch window, where these `-next` packages are; `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on the head. **Right.**
- ADR-0087 disposition: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a member of `CATEGORIES` in `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, with the why stated (no spec key, authorable spelling or stored shape moves; what narrows is a runtime accept set; the remedy is an access decision on the parent, not a rewrite). Nothing an author can write is removed or renamed, so no FROM-to-TO mapping is owed. **Right.**
- The changeset body names the one changed answer and the remedy direction. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

The os-dev report's `deviations`, each answered:
- Pre-edit empty-branch push refused by the container's classifier; the first push came after the fix sat on red pins — a process note with no effect on the diff. Answered.
- The real-stack differential ran on a scratch harness, never committed — the committed pins are doubles; acceptable under the disclosure ruling, since a concrete fixture would read as a reproduction. Answered; see the second open question.
- Attachment parity rows in the existing test file rather than a new one, to drive the ledgered engine double — right; the ledger gate is green. Answered.
- `plugin-security` not edited — right; the claim made that surface conditional and the measurement found no divergence to fix there. Answered.
- The `403 FILES_DISABLED` to `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` changed answer — declared in the changeset, the body and the docs; judged in ① item 5. Answered.
- The public report omits the seat-only divergence field — right under the disclosure order. Answered.
- Model-free commit trailers — right per AGENTS.md. Answered.
- Gate runs overlapping the ablation window, nine commands re-run — a process note; the check-runs on this head are the verdicts. Answered.

The report's `open_questions`, each judged and escalated:
- **Edit depth on the parent.** The gates keep the sharing step at `own`, so on a caller whose edit depth on the parent is wider than `own` the gate refuses where the parent's by-id update and `explain` admit; the card's acceptance bullets 1 and 2 and its bullet 3 pull apart on exactly those rows, in the restrictive direction. Keeping the ruled step inside a p1 security fix is right: the #7144 ruling binds until a superseding ruling says otherwise, and lifting it widens who may moderate. Escalated to the seat: whether the gates may drop the own-depth step and let the update judgement decide alone is the maintainer's ruling to make, on its own card; this PR does not reopen it.
- **Where the real-stack parity pins live.** Shipping abstract unit pins per gate plus plugin-security's explain-parity suite is right while the disclosure hold stands. Escalated to the seat: a real-stack pin inside the gate packages (two devDependencies and the lockfile, outside this claim's surface) is a follow-up once the maintainer lifts the hold, so a regression to either gate is caught where it is made.

The report's `out_of_scope_findings`:
- One row where `explain`'s update verdict refuses and the by-id update admits (restrictive; not a hole) — report-only, carrier plugin-security's explain-enforce-parity table; the concrete row is held off GitHub. Escalated to the seat: it is a contract violation of the explain-equals-enforce promise and owes a card under Prime Directive #10, in the redacted filing shape the triage seat used on this card.
- The attachments docs page — discharged at the head (commit e1fdd691e).

Further flags from this review:
- **PR body drift, two sentences — the seat refreshes the body.** The Files section says the changeset is `patch` for both packages (the head carries `minor`), and the last acceptance note says the docs edit lies outside the claim's surface (the head carries it, as the claim's file surface allowed at the review of record). The committed tree is right; the gates read the changeset, not the prose.
- **Hook-order dependency on the unknown-parent-object answer** (① item 5): not pinned by the diff. Nothing owed on this card; noted so that a later ordering change is read as a changed answer, not a regression.
- **Parity is bounded by `explain`'s record path.** `security-plugin.ts` documents that the delegated (on-behalf-of) envelope keeps its previous inputs on explain's record path and is not fully modelled there. On that envelope shape the gate is exactly as narrow as before plus the new step, so the hole is not widened; whether it is fully closed there is a property of `explain` — the existing explain-versus-enforce boundary — not of this diff. Noted for the seat; nothing owed here.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24549-parent-gate-parity`
Reviewed-by: `session_01LR1cD9JqgkeqY7k9rrZH8s`

**VERDICT: PASS**
